conviction_note: Evidence roughly offsets. XPEL has beaten the top of its own revenue guide in 2 of the last 3 quarters while Q3 consensus sits at the guide midpoint; set against that are a weaker China aftermarket and a Q4 guide that has to lap the China acquisition. abs_move 9.0 comes from the name's median 9.54% reaction, trimmed because the option chain is unusable. p_up 49 because the negatives are proxies or inference and a 10.7%-of-float short with 13 days to cover argues against leaning short. The findings sum to -0.8 and the scaled number is -0.18. They agree in sign and differ only because p_up near 50 compresses the scaled number.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue guide of ~$137-139m, from the company's Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm, 2026-08-05). Benzinga consensus is $138.4m revenue and $0.61 EPS (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/XPEL/earnings-forecasts). EPS is disputed: Earnings Whispers has $0.55 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/xpel). No finding is sized on EPS. Q4 consensus is $132.9m revenue (Benzinga, a single source).
positioning_check: Short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement was 2.67M shares, 10.72% of float and 13.2 days to cover, up 4.65% on the prior report (Chartmill via search snippet, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/XPEL/ownership/short-interest). On 2026-08-19 it was 8.85% and 11.7 days (https://equibles.com/stocks/xpel/shortinterest). This is a fairly crowded short relative to 187k shares of average daily volume. Skew is -15.3 vol points (upside paid), but the ATM bid-ask spread is 90% of mid, so the chain says little. The stock is 22% below its 52-week high and down 5.1% over 20 days.

findings.finding: XPEL usually beats the top of its own guide: Q1 2026 came in at $117.4m against a $112-114m guide (+3.0% over the top) and Q2 2026 at $143.1m against $135-137m (+4.5%), Q4 2025 being the exception at $122.3m against $123-125m. The Q3 bar of $137-139m and Benzinga's $138.4m consensus sit at the midpoint, not at the usual beat. Management said about $1-2m of Q3 sales were pulled into Q2, which trims the likely beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a 4.5% beat over the top of the guide with gross margin up bought +9.54%. Q1 2026: a 3% beat sold -11.83% on the Q2 guide and margin caveats. Q4 2025: a miss against the guide sold -6.86%. So a revenue beat alone has not been enough.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected the habitual 3-4% beat, consensus would sit near $142-143m rather than at the $138.4m guide midpoint, and the stock would not be down 5% over 20 days and 22% off its high.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 beat: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260506705719/en/ ; Q4 2025 miss: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1767258/000176725826000007/xpelye2025earnings.htm . All three come from company documents, so they are one pattern.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CEO said XPEL would implement 'relatively modest price increases in some regions during Q3'. That supports Q3 revenue and the gross margin he guided to 'continue to modestly increase' from 44.1%. Competitor Eastman said performance films improved price-cost in 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin expansion (42.9% to 44.1%) accompanied the +9.54% Q2 reaction. In Q1 the margin outlook was hedged as 'not guaranteed' and the stock fell 11.83%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the decision came before the guide was set, so it is likely inside the $137-139m guide. Only the margin flow-through is uncertain.
findings.independence: Eastman Q3 2026 prepared remarks: 'performance films improved price cost' (https://s29.q4cdn.com/397220757/files/content_files/Eastman-Q3-2026-Prepared-Comments.pdf).

findings.finding: Eastman, a direct PPF and window-film competitor (LLumar/SunTek), reported on 2026-10-29, after XPEL last spoke. Its performance-films volume fell sequentially in Q3 on 'continued weakness in the automotive market, particularly in China', and 'the aftermarket for performance films remained challenged in an already very weak domestic Chinese auto market'. CPCA's final September China retail was 1.618m, down 28% year on year, against roughly -20% in Q2 per XPEL's CEO and -24% in August. XPEL China was $15.9m (11% of revenue) in Q2, and the guide assumed 'consistent' APAC trends.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: China has not been a stated driver of past reactions. In Q2 the region grew 106.7%, largely from the acquisition, alongside the +9.54% move. No prior China miss is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Eastman's remarks came after XPEL's guide and nobody has re-cut XPEL estimates since (no rating or estimate changes found for September-October). If it were priced, consensus would sit below the $138.4m midpoint. Net of the rest of the company, the US (55% of revenue) grew 11.7% in Q2 and a $1-1.5m China shortfall is about 1% of revenue, so the finding is small.
findings.independence: CPCA September retail: https://www.marklines.com/en/report/cpca084_202610 and https://www.just-auto.com/newsletters/chinas-pv-retail-sales-plunge-28-in-september . A different source from Eastman. XPEL's own Q2 call said the China domestic market was down about 20% year on year (https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2946562).

findings.finding: The Q4 guide must lap the China distributor acquisition: Q4 2025 already carried $14.0m of China revenue (+51.9% year on year) against minimal China contribution in Q3 2025. Ex-China, Q2 2026 grew about 8.7% ($127.2m against $117.0m). On that rate with China flat to down in a -20-28% market, Q4 2026 comes to roughly $129.5-131.6m. Benzinga's Q4 consensus is $132.9m, and XPEL habitually guides below consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the Q3 guide of $137-139m was below the $139.1-141.3m consensus and the stock still rose 9.54% on the beat. May 2026: the Q2 guide plus a margin hedge brought -11.83%. February 2026: the Q1 guide of $112-114m alongside a Q4 miss brought -6.86%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $132.9m implies 8.7% growth, the same as the ex-China organic rate, which only works if China holds flat in a market down 20-28%. If the lap were priced, Q4 consensus would sit near $130m. This is my arithmetic, not a company statement, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: The Q2 2026 regional table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm) supplies the ex-China growth rate. It shares the China-market premise with the Eastman/CPCA finding, but this one lands on the guide and that one on the quarter.

findings.finding: US new-vehicle demand softened late in the quarter: September SAAR was 16.0m, down 3.5% month on month and 3.7% year on year, and Edmunds forecast Q3 volume 0.7% below Q3 2025. The US was 55% of XPEL revenue and grew 11.7% in Q2 against a roughly flat market, and the CEO cited continued dealership challenges ('FTC concerns').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US grew double digits through a flat SAAR in 2025-26, and the market has not traded XPEL on SAAR prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Barely unpriced: SAAR is public. It is a macro-to-company proxy that XPEL has repeatedly outgrown, hence the small size.
findings.independence: Edmunds Q3 forecast: https://www.edmunds.com/press/new-vehicle-sales-expected-to-dip-slightly-in-q3-amid-economic-headwinds-according-to-edmunds.html . Proxy only; XPEL has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Tesla, an OEM and aftermarket channel for XPEL, delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026. That beat Tesla's compiled consensus of 461,974 but was about 2% below the 497,099 of Q3 2025, a quarter flattered by the US tax-credit pull-forward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None recorded. Tesla was not mentioned on XPEL's Q2 call.
findings.why_not_priced: Public datapoint. XPEL's Tesla exposure is not disclosed, so it is a proxy and sized near zero.

findings.finding: Eastman's 2026-10-29 remarks say the Middle East conflict escalated during Q3 and was its primary driver of sequential decline, with Gulf order-fulfilment problems. XPEL's India and Middle East region ($6.4m, -5% in Q2) was hit by vehicle shortages, but the Q3 guide explicitly assumed no recapture of that business.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Middle East vehicle shortages were cited around the May 2026 print (-11.83%) alongside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide, because management excluded recapture ('we're not expecting really any of that recapture', https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2946562). Only a further decline below the Q2 run-rate is unpriced.
findings.independence: Shares the Eastman document with the China finding. Separate Brent/Hormuz escalation coverage: https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2026/09/08/brent-hits-six-week-high-middle-east-conflict-escalates/

findings.finding: Short interest rose into the print: 10.72% of float and 13.2 days to cover at 2026-09-30 (up 4.65% on the prior report), against 8.85% and 11.7 days in August, while the stock sits 22% below its 52-week high.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 the shares rose 9.54% on a beat that came with a below-consensus guide, which fits short covering into a beat.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-30 settlement (via search snippet; page returned 403 to fetch)
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the bet, not information. It asymmetrically amplifies a beat (13 days to cover on 187k average daily volume), and this raises the upside tail more than the mean.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filings since 2026-08-05: only routine director RSU vesting Form 4s (2026-09-10 North, 2026-10-05 Crumly), two 13G/As and a July 30 director resignation for an employer policy; no 8-K outside the print
Analyst rating and price-target changes in September-October 2026: none found (last was B. Riley raising to $65 on 2026-08-06)
XPEL press releases in October 2026 other than the call notice: none
IEEPA tariff refund exposure in XPEL's Q2 10-Q: none disclosed
Public announcement of XPEL price increases or dealer pre-buying: none beyond the call comment

rejected_candidates.candidate: Benzinga's statement that XPEL 'raised' the Q3 guide from $135-137m to $137-139m in August
rejected_candidates.detail: The Q2 8-K gives Q3 guidance once ($137-139m) and the $135-137m range was the Q2 guide, so this is an aggregator mislabel.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Freedom Broker downgrade to Hold with a $45 target, citing a cautious outlook
rejected_candidates.detail: No date could be established for the note, so it may predate the window.

baseline_tension: The upside-paid skew (-15 vol points) would agree with the beat-habit and short-squeeze findings, but the chain's 90% ATM spread makes it close to meaningless. The China and Q4-guide negatives cut against the skew and are inference or proxy, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short, 10.7% of float, 13 days to cover): China/films negative cut from -1.2 to -1.0 and the Q4-guide negative from -1.0 to -0.8.
Lesson 6 (a finding inside what the company guided): the price-increase finding cut from +0.4 to +0.2, and the Middle East finding from -0.3 to -0.1 because the guide excluded recapture.
Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; beats have been sold before, -11.83% in May): the beat-habit finding cut from +1.2 to +1.0.
Lessons 5 and 9 (proxy sizing; net of the rest of the company): the SAAR and Tesla proxies stay small and the China finding is sized net of the 55% US base. No change to abs_move_pct or p_up.
